project.name: ilovehust
project.description: ILoveHust is a TypeScript full-stack student support web app for HUST students, covering profiles, grades, schedules, tasks, forum, messaging, and realtime notifications.

nodes.name: App.tsx
nodes.summary: React Router application shell that maps public auth routes and student feature routes to their page components.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses React Router route elements to centralize client-side navigation.

nodes.name: api.ts
nodes.summary: Configures the shared Axios client with the API base URL and bearer-token request interceptor used by frontend pages.

nodes.name: language.ts
nodes.summary: Provides localStorage-backed language and student sidebar preference helpers shared across auth and student pages.

nodes.name: main.tsx
nodes.summary: Frontend bootstrap that mounts the React app into the DOM and loads the central stylesheet.

nodes.name: Login.tsx
nodes.summary: Implements the login screen, credential validation, auth API call, language selection, token persistence, and profile-completion redirect.
nodes.languageNotes: Large React page component with localized UI text and inline auth workflow handlers.

nodes.name: Register.tsx
nodes.summary: Implements the registration screen with localized validation, account creation, token persistence, and redirect into student profile completion.
nodes.languageNotes: Combines form validation and API submission inside a single exported React page component.

nodes.name: CompleteProfile.tsx
nodes.summary: Implements the multi-step student profile completion workflow, loading current user and major data before submitting academic profile details.
nodes.languageNotes: Large stateful React page with nested async loading and step validation handlers.

nodes.name: Grades.tsx
nodes.summary: Implements the student grades dashboard, including grade search/filtering, summary visualization helpers, PDF export preparation, and student layout integration.
nodes.languageNotes: Defines local SVG chart helpers alongside the main React page.

nodes.name: Schedule.tsx
nodes.summary: Implements the student schedule calendar with date navigation, week/month views, custom event creation, localized labels, and student layout integration.
nodes.languageNotes: Contains date formatting helpers and calendar layout calculations near the page component.

nodes.name: App
nodes.summary: Defines the top-level BrowserRouter route table for auth and student-facing pages.

nodes.name: Dashboard.tsx

nodes.languageNotes: Uses React state/effects with inline SVG chart rendering and localized task date formatting.

nodes.summary: Normalizes task due labels into localized dashboard display text, preserving already-localized today labels and formatting ISO dates.

nodes.name: Dashboard

nodes.name: Forum.tsx

nodes.name: MessagesPage

nodes.name: studentNavigation.ts
nodes.summary: Centralizes student sidebar route mapping, logout session cleanup, and navigation behavior shared by student pages.

nodes.name: StudentTaskbar
nodes.summary: Renders the localized student navigation rail, secondary settings/logout actions, overlay close control, and AI chat shortcut.

nodes.name: translations.ts
nodes.summary: Centralizes bilingual and localized UI copy for the frontend, including taskbar, header, dashboard, grades, authentication, profile, tasks, statistics, schedule, forum, and messaging text.
nodes.languageNotes: Large TypeScript constant module with many named exports and no runtime logic.

nodes.name: Settings.tsx
nodes.summary: Implements the student settings page for loading profile data, editing contact and academic fields, uploading avatars, and persisting language/sidebar preferences.
nodes.languageNotes: Single large React page component combines data loading, form validation, file upload, localStorage synchronization, and layout composition.

nodes.name: SettingsPage
nodes.summary: Coordinates the settings workflow, including authenticated profile fetches, avatar preview/upload, profile update validation, menu navigation, and responsive student layout rendering.

nodes.name: Statistics.tsx
nodes.summary: Builds the student statistics dashboard with API-backed GPA, credits, study time, achievements, goals, and cohort comparison visualizations.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Recharts components and memoized localized datasets to render multiple academic analytics views.

nodes.name: StatisticsPage
nodes.summary: Loads authenticated statistics data, localizes chart/card labels, manages page errors and preferences, and renders academic performance charts in the student shell.

nodes.name: Tasks.tsx
nodes.summary: Implements the student tasks page with task loading, filtering, search, pagination, create/edit modal handling, optimistic completion, deletion, and progress statistics.
nodes.languageNotes: React page combines debounced search, IntersectionObserver-based loading, optimistic updates, and localized task labels.

nodes.name: TasksPage
nodes.summary: Coordinates authenticated task list retrieval, filter/search state, infinite loading, task create/update/delete actions, completion animation, and the task modal UI.

layers.description: Project manifests, TypeScript/Vite/Vercel settings, environment examples, and local tool configuration used to build and deploy the app.

layers.name: Documentation
layers.description: Repository guidance and project documentation covering setup, API contracts, database structure, and UI rules.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the README to understand ILoveHust as a student support web app for HUST students. It frames the major product areas: profile, grades, schedules, tasks, forum, messaging, notifications, and local/deploy setup.

tour.title: Frontend Boot Path
tour.description: The frontend starts in main.tsx and hands control to App.tsx, where React Router defines the major screens. This shows how users move from login and registration into dashboard, grades, forum, messages, tasks, schedule, statistics, and settings pages.

tour.title: Client API Boundary
tour.description: The Axios wrapper centralizes API calls and bearer-token injection so page components do not repeat authentication plumbing. Understanding this file explains how frontend views communicate with the Express backend consistently.

tour.title: Backend Server
tour.description: The Express server wires CORS, JSON parsing, static uploads, REST route modules, environment validation, and Socket.IO initialization. This is the backend runtime map: every HTTP feature hangs off the route mounts declared here.

tour.title: Authentication And Data
tour.description: Authentication middleware verifies JWTs, rejects inactive accounts, and attaches the current user to protected requests. The Prisma client module connects route logic to PostgreSQL through the Prisma PG adapter, making these files the core request-to-database bridge.
tour.languageLesson: Express middleware composes request processing by adding checks and context before route handlers run. Prisma schema files define the TypeScript client surface and the database model from one source of truth.

tour.title: Student Features
tour.description: The student route module owns dashboard data, task CRUD, statistics, grades, profile updates, and avatar upload. Pair it with the forum, message, and schedule route modules to see how the app splits user-facing features while preserving shared auth and database patterns.

tour.title: Realtime Notifications
tour.description: Socket.IO authenticates clients with the same JWT concept as HTTP and joins each user to a private room. Notification helpers create deduped database notifications, while the frontend socket client connects with the stored token to receive realtime updates.

tour.title: Database Evolution
tour.description: The Prisma schema describes the current domain model, and SQL migrations capture how that model evolved over time. These migrations add forum, task, chat, attachment, schedule, notification, and event end-time support, which explains why the route modules have the data shapes they do.
tour.languageLesson: Database migrations are ordered change records. They let the schema evolve incrementally while preserving a reproducible path from an empty database to the current model.

tour.title: Project Contracts
tour.description: The API and UI documentation record the contracts that future changes should preserve. Use these after reading the code paths to understand expected route behavior, database assumptions, and frontend conventions.
